predecessors.name: Maya city-states (Postclassic)
predecessors.text: the site core of Chichen Itza, 'at least 5 square kilometers', with its hinterland

successors.name: Mayapan
successors.text: Page: a regional capital 'controlling the area from central Yucatan to the north coast' in the 10th century; Isla Cerritos 'established ... as a trading port'.

ledger.x: c. 900: Chichen Itza, a Late Classic town founded by local Maya with the Itza 'arriving around 800 AD', becomes a regional capital ('between 900 and 1050 AD it expanded to become a powerful regional capital'; prominent already 'roughly 600 AD').

10th century: Chichen Itza 'a regional capital controlling the area from central Yucatan to the north coast', establishes Isla Cerritos as a port and outlasts Yaxuna and Coba, whose collapse it 'may have directly contributed to'; the Coba page adds that Chichen Itza 'gained…

By 1100: 'Chichen Itza declined as a regional center by 1100, before the rise of Mayapan'; the Chilam Balam chronicles have Hunac Ceel of Mayapan 'conquered Chichen Itza in the 13th century', which the page doubts.

certainty.note: No frontier is described; the radius is a reading of 'central Yucatan to the north coast'.
